# Routing evaluation of the deployed decision engine (generated by RoutingEvaluationTest)

> **Synthetic data.** The 613 rows are the held-out test split of a template-generated, author-annotated dataset (ml/data/notifications.csv). These numbers show how the pipeline behaves on that data. They are **not** real-world accuracy, and nothing here was tuned on the test split by this report.

Engine = model + safety rules + guard layer (urgent wording, burst, redaction, priority, link). Model-only = the route ml/train.py reports. Mapping: ALLOW=DELIVER, HOLD=DEFER/FILTER, REVIEW=REVIEW. Focus session, every category queued, no user rules, no personalization.

### Link analysis (separate from importance), all 3105 rows

Rule-based and untrained. Gold labels come from the old, coarser Python rules (caution = risky ending or brand look-alike), so disagreement is expected where the new rules are stricter (shorteners) or more selective (an unusual ending alone).

| gold \ new analyzer | none | unknown | caution | high_risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 2889 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| unknown | 0 | 138 | 30 | 0 |
| caution | 0 | 7 | 3 | 38 |

### Train/test leakage check

- Templates shared between train and test: **0** (the split is grouped by template).
- Test rows whose text token set is >= 0.8 similar (Jaccard, digits/links normalised) to some training row: 2.0% (12/613); >= 0.9: 2.0% (12/613); identical: 2.0% (12/613).
- Near-identical wording across *different* templates inflates scores; this is a known weakness of the synthetic set (see ml/README.md).

- Rows held by the engine that the model-only route kept visible (link-neutral reading): 7; gold labels of those rows: {defer=7}
